messages:
Lena Fischer: seeing a perf regression in staging after the bounded-queue change landed (ENG-4826 / PR-18475). decode p99 is up ~18–25% on the perf-canary “short chat” scenario. anyone else seeing this?

perf-canary bot: perf-canary report: `runtime/scheduler` regression detected
- scenario: `step_traffic_short_chat`
- baseline commit: 9c2a1f1
- current commit: 3e7d4b8
- p50: +2.3%
- p95: +9.8%
- p99: +22.4%
- shed_rate: 0.0% (no shedding)
- queue_wait_ms p99: 41ms -> 133ms
link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary/runtime?var_scenario=step_traffic_short_chat

Marcus Reed: :eyes: looking. bounded queue shouldn’t add queue_wait when we’re not shedding. maybe we’re hitting the new “admission pause” path more often?

Sofia Ivanova: do we have a trace slice? curious if scheduler is spending time in lock contention on the queue struct.

Lena Fischer: quick trace sample from staging (10 reqs) shows more time in `enqueue()` + `try_schedule()`.
```
span: runtime.scheduler.enqueue
p99: 1.8ms -> 7.4ms
span: runtime.scheduler.pick_next
p99: 3.1ms -> 5.9ms
span: runtime.gpu.dispatch_prefill
unchanged
```
I also see `queue_depth` hovering at 70–90 (max=100) even under moderate load.

Noah Patel: if it’s hovering near max without actual overload, we might be underestimating “in flight” capacity with the new accounting. are we counting streaming decode tokens as queued?

Marcus Reed: PR-18475 changed the queue to include “work items” not “requests” (prefill item + decode item). if a single request becomes multiple items, max=100 is effectively smaller. that could inflate depth.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. long prompts / streaming will produce more decode slices. if we’re splitting decode into chunks, queue stays full and we’re effectively round-robin’ing too hard.

Sofia Ivanova: what’s the intended scheduling granularity? if decode is chunked per N tokens, we might be bouncing between requests too frequently and thrashing caches.

Lena Fischer: current config in staging:
- decode quantum = 16 tokens
- max_queue_items = 100
- max_inflight_prefills = 8
- max_inflight_decodes = 32
We didn’t change decode quantum, but the queue now holds decode work items explicitly.

Vikram Singh: fwiw gateway/routing is fine, nothing changed there. this looks runtime-only.

Caleb Johnson: do we have a metric for “queue item type” breakdown? (prefill vs decode). if decode items dominate, that’d match the depth behavior.

Marcus Reed: we added `runtime_queue_items{type=...}` behind a flag but I think it’s off in staging :/ I can flip it in canary env if folks are ok.

Noah Patel: ok to flip in canary. also, can we sanity check if `max_queue_items` should scale with `(prefill + decode)` rather than being a fixed number?

Sofia Ivanova: I’d rather keep a fixed upper bound for protection, but we can tune it. maybe:
- cap prefills separately
- cap decodes separately
so decode churn doesn’t block prefills.

Omar El-Sayed: ^ yes. prefills are latency sensitive + unblock streaming. if decode queue is full, prefills waiting is worst case.

Lena Fischer: another datapoint: p99 `time_to_first_token` up 12% in the same run. aligns with prefills waiting.

Marcus Reed: so two likely culprits:
1) max_queue_items too low now that we count work items
2) queue fairness change causing too many context switches (decode quantum?)

Noah Patel: any easy mitigation for today? we’ve got a canary enablement planned soon and don’t want to drag a regression along.

Sofia Ivanova: short-term: bump `max_queue_items` in staging from 100 -> 250 and see if queue_wait drops. should be safe; still bounded.

Omar El-Sayed: and/or increase decode quantum from 16 -> 32 tokens to reduce churn. risk: can increase tail for mixed workloads, but might help overall throughput.

Lena Fischer: I can run a quick A/B on perf-canary:
A) max_queue_items=250
B) decode_quantum=32
C) both

Marcus Reed: I’ll prep a follow-up PR to separate caps by type (prefill/decode) + adjust default queue limit to reflect work items. target: small + low risk.

Noah Patel: please do. also document in the PR description why this didn’t show up in unit tests (because they use non-streaming + short prompts).

Caleb Johnson: if you want, I can add a panel to perf-canary dashboard for `queue_wait_ms` and `queue_items` breakdown once the metric flag is on.

Lena Fischer: ran A/B (first pass, 3 iterations each):
- A (max_queue_items=250): p99 improved from +22% -> +6% vs baseline
- B (decode_quantum=32): p99 improved to +12%
- C (both): p99 now +3% (basically noise)
TTFT p99 also back near baseline under A/C.

Sofia Ivanova: that’s pretty conclusive. we should bump the default in config and still keep the bound. the separate caps are a nicer longer-term fix.

Marcus Reed: made follow-up PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18506
- increases default `max_queue_items` from 100 -> 250 (only for hosted runtime profiles)
- adds `max_prefill_queue_items` (default 64) + `max_decode_queue_items` (default 256) behind `runtime.queue_split_caps`
- adds metric `runtime_queue_items{type=prefill|decode}` enabled by default in staging

Lena Fischer: :thumbsup: (reactions: Sofia Ivanova :thumbsup:, Omar El-Sayed :thumbsup:)

Noah Patel: thanks. let’s do:
1) merge PR-18506 behind a runtime flag
2) enable in staging + perf-canary
3) if stable for 24h, roll into canary alongside the bounded queue feature flag

Omar El-Sayed: one more thing: when queue is near full, do we currently prioritize finishing in-flight decodes vs admitting new prefills? we should ensure prefills aren’t starved.

Sofia Ivanova: PR-18506 notes “prefill reserved slots” (nice). let’s confirm behavior in the scheduler: prefills should be able to proceed as long as prefill cap isn’t hit, regardless of decode backlog.

Marcus Reed: yep, scheduler change in PR-18506: decode backlog no longer blocks prefill enqueue until prefill cap is full. left a comment with pseudocode.

Caleb Johnson: I’ll update the dashboard + add alert annotation for `queue_wait_ms p99` during canary runs once metrics are in.

Lena Fischer: I’ll re-run full suite tonight and post results in this thread. if we’re within +/-5% across scenarios, I’m comfortable.

Noah Patel: +1. also please add a short note in ENG-4826 that the queue bound changed semantics (work items vs requests) so folks don’t reintroduce this later.

Marcus Reed: will do. also adding a regression test that asserts “no-shed moderate load” keeps queue_wait < 50ms p99.

Lena Fischer: closing the loop: full suite results with PR-18506 + config A (max_queue_items=250) in staging:
- short_chat p99: +2.1%
- long_prompt_spike p99: +4.8%
- streaming_mix TTFT p99: -1.3% (slightly better)
No new errors. queue_wait p99 back to ~55ms.

Sofia Ivanova: :shipit: (reactions: Noah Patel :shipit:)

Noah Patel: great. proceed with rollout plan. if any surprise on customer workloads, we can revert config without dropping bounded-queue protection.
